verses.1: These are the descendants of the sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. They each had sons after the flood.
verses.2: The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
verses.3: The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
verses.4: The sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
verses.5: From these the island-dwelling nations separated, each to their own lands, by their language, in their families, by their nations.
verses.6: The sons of Ham were Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan.
verses.7: The sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
verses.8: Cush fathered Nimrod, who became a mighty man on the earth.
verses.9: He was a mighty hunter before the LORD. That is why it is said, “Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD.”
verses.10: The beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
verses.11: From that land, Assyria went out and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah.
verses.12: And Resen, between Nineveh and Calah—that is the great city.
verses.13: The sons of Egypt were Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphthuhim,
verses.14: Pathrusim, Casluhim (from whom the Philistines came), and Caphtorim.
verses.15: Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,
verses.16: and the Jebusites, the Amorites, and the Girgashites,
verses.17: the Hivites, the Arkites, and the Sinites,
verses.18: the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Later, the clans of the Canaanites dispersed.
verses.19: The boundary of the Canaanites extended from Sidon as far as Gerar, to Gaza, as far as Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
verses.20: These are the sons of Ham, by their families, by their languages, in their lands, by their nations.
verses.21: Shem, too, had sons born to him, and he became the father of all the sons of Eber, the older brother of Japheth.
verses.22: The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
verses.23: The sons of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
verses.24: Arpachshad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
verses.25: To Eber were born two sons. The name of one was Peleg, for in his time the earth was divided. His brother’s name was Joktan.
verses.26: Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
verses.29: Ofir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
verses.30: Their settlements extended from Mesha as far as Sephar, the mountain east of the desert.
verses.31: These are the sons of Shem, by their families, by their languages, in their lands, by their nations.
verses.32: These are the families of the sons of Noah, by their generations, by their nations. From these the nations dispersed on the earth after the flood.

notes:
Notes
- v. 5: "island-dwelling nations" reflects "אִיֵּי הַגּוֹיִם" (islands of the nations), referring to seafaring or coastal peoples.
- v. 9: "before the LORD" is likely metaphorical, referring to being recognized or feared by people rather than a divine favor.
- v. 15: "Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn" — "firstborn" is added for clarity, though Hebrew does not use the word for "firstborn" (בְּכֹר) here; it is implied.
- v. 25: "Peleg" is interpreted as meaning "division," and the phrase "in his time the earth was divided" reflects the naming rationale in context.
- v. 30: "mountain east of the desert" is a contextual rendering of "הַקֶּֽדֶם" (the East), referring to the general region east of the Arabian desert.

[1] These are the descendants of the sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. They each had sons after the flood.

[2] The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

[3] The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.

[4] The sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

[5] From these the island-dwelling nations separated, each to their own lands, by their language, in their families, by their nations.

[6] The sons of Ham were Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan.

[7] The sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.

[8] Cush fathered Nimrod, who became a mighty man on the earth.

[9] He was a mighty hunter before the LORD. That is why it is said, “Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD.”

[10] The beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.

[11] From that land, Assyria went out and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah.

[12] And Resen, between Nineveh and Calah—that is the great city.

[13] The sons of Egypt were Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphthuhim,

[14] Pathrusim, Casluhim (from whom the Philistines came), and Caphtorim.

[15] Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,

[16] and the Jebusites, the Amorites, and the Girgashites,

[17] the Hivites, the Arkites, and the Sinites,

[18] the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Later, the clans of the Canaanites dispersed.

[19] The boundary of the Canaanites extended from Sidon as far as Gerar, to Gaza, as far as Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.

[20] These are the sons of Ham, by their families, by their languages, in their lands, by their nations.

[21] Shem, too, had sons born to him, and he became the father of all the sons of Eber, the older brother of Japheth.

[22] The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.

[23] The sons of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.

[24] Arpachshad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.

[25] To Eber were born two sons. The name of one was Peleg, for in his time the earth was divided. His brother’s name was Joktan.

[26] Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

[27] Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,

[28] Obal, Abimael, and Sheba,

[29] Ofir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.

[30] Their settlements extended from Mesha as far as Sephar, the mountain east of the desert.

[31] These are the sons of Shem, by their families, by their languages, in their lands, by their nations.

[32] These are the families of the sons of Noah, by their generations, by their nations. From these the nations dispersed on the earth after the flood.
